name: A year of a GST-registered New Zealand trading company, filing two-monthly on the invoice and payments bases, for the year ended 31 December 2027

contacts.name: Private buyer — not a taxable activity

documents.why: A standard taxable sale on the invoice basis: the GST-exclusive value posts to the hidden box 5B and the GST to the hidden box 5T, which sum to Box 5 of the GST101A.
A creditable purchase of trading stock: box 11B takes the value and 11T the credit, which sum to Box 11 and are worked into Box 12.
A retail sale on a GST-inclusive price: the engine takes 3/23 out of 1,150.00, exactly 150.00 of GST on a 1,000.00 base.
A zero-rated export of goods under s. 11(1)(a): Box 5 and Box 6 both take the value, and the invoice carries the zero-rating sentence.
A zero-rated supply of services to a non-resident outside New Zealand under s. 11A(1): Box 5 and Box 6, and the EN 16931 category is G, the one PINT A-NZ gives an export.

A purchase relating to the exempt residential letting (s. 20(3) and s. 21): no credit, so the 15 % GST becomes part of the cost through tax_on_base, and the value is kept out of Box 11 because no credit is claimed on it.

An ordinary taxable purchase in the same period as the zero-rated and exempt documents above, so the busiest period by document count is also one where a real GST account moves — printing for the shop.
Residential rent, exempt under s. 14(1)(c): not included in the GST return at all, and the invoice carries the exempt sentence.

lines.name: Rent of Flat 3, Ponsonby — March quarter

documents.why: The sale of the taxable activity as a going concern, zero-rated under s. 11(1)(m): Box 5 and Box 6 take the whole price.

lines.name: Sale of the retail taxable activity as a going concern

documents.why: The sale of land to another GST-registered person acquiring it for taxable supplies, compulsorily zero-rated under s. 11(1)(mb): Box 5 and Box 6.

lines.name: Sale of the Kestrel Bay warehouse site

documents.why: An offshore software subscription reverse charged under s. 8(4B) because it serves the exempt residential letting (taxable use assumed below 95 %): the self-assessed GST lands on 2100 through box 5B and 5T exactly as an ordinary sale's output tax would, and the whole of it is also a cost of the acquisition through tax_on_base — no credit at all.
A sale accounted for on the payments basis (s. 20(3), below the $2,000,000 threshold): nothing in period P3, and all of it in period P5 when the customer pays.
A credit note on S1 for two returned units: box 5B and 5T, and Box 5 with them, go down in the period it is issued.
A purchase accounted for on the payments basis: the credit waits on 1152 and reaches box 11T in period P6, when the invoice is paid.
A zero-rated purchase: the supplier charged no GST, so there is none to claim, and the value is kept out of Box 11.
An exempt purchase — bank account fees under s. 14: Box 11 takes nothing.
A credit note received on P1: box 11B and 11T, and Box 11 and Box 12 with them, go down.
Council rates: a statutory charge with no GST in the price, kept out of Box 11.
Interest on a related-party loan, an exempt financial service under s. 14(1)(a): not included in the GST return.

lines.name: Interest on advance to Totara Retail Group

documents.why: A sale outside the course or furtherance of any taxable activity: no GST and no box at all.

lines.name: Sale of a private motor vehicle

documents.why: A second taxable sale, in the final period, so period P6 carries output tax and a positive Box 15.

payments.why: A receipt that settles S1 exactly.
A payment that settles P1 exactly.
The receipt that moves the GST of S8 (payments basis) into the period it is actually recognised, September–October 2027.
The payment that moves the credit of P4 (payments basis) into November–December 2027.
A payment on account that matches no invoice and stays open.
